text:
maria: Heads up — two customer restores failed with DecryptError around 03:40 UTC during last CMK rotation. Snapshots show SSE metadata missing on a couple of multipart parts. Anyone seen this pattern?

alex: Can you paste the snapshot object metadata + any KMS grant logs you have?

maria: Pasting minimal logs and snapshot meta. saw grant create at 03:39:52 then snapshot object written at 03:40:01. snippet:
```
restore_id=rcv-17a
snapshot=tenant-prod-2026-03-23-0339
object.metadata: {sse: "aws:kms", key_id: "cmk-0a1b2c", parts: 3}
encops-bot: grant_create key=cmk-0a1b2c principal=uploader svcacct time=2026-03-23T03:39:52Z
kms_response: grant_ack=true
object.write start=2026-03-23T03:40:01Z
```

nishant: That timing smells like a propagation/race window. If uploader started multipart put before the grant fully propagated to the storage proxy or the agent that writes SSE headers, the header may be omitted for early parts. We've hit similar with ephemeral grants before.

pete: Also check if the uploader agent rotated its role or temporary creds right around that time. We had a brief IAM sync job redeploy at 03:38 in staging historically that caused header drops. Does the object show `sse` missing on part-1 only or multiple?

maria: Missing on part-1 + part-3 in both restores. full object-level metadata shows `sse: aws:kms` but individual multipart manifest lacks per-part encryption header for those parts.

encops-bot: alert: replicate-grant-delay metric spike at 03:39:55 -> https://internal/alerts/replicate-grant-delay/1739054321 (FYI, auto-run diagnostics queued) :warning:

sre-oncall: FYI tagging this as P2 and adding to incident board. immediate mitigation options: 1) hold restores/writes until grant confirmations are present, 2) fallback to previous CMK for decryption (if allowed), 3) re-run upload/part rewrite to attach sse metadata.

pete: Short-term mitigation: add an extra grant-check RPC in the uploader before initiating multipart for any CMK recently rotated (<= 2m). Not ideal but should cut this class of failures. We'll need to make it idempotent.

nishant: Long-term: extend auditchain to record `key_id` + `grant_tx_id` into object metadata and our snapshot manifest. That gives us deterministic proof of which key/grant was expected and lets us auto-detect discrepancies at restore time. Also add a small tracing header so we can correlate grant creation -> storage ack.

sam: I can run a replay on staging with forced grant propagation lag and verify fixes. Scheduling for 13:00 PT. Will post results. :thumbsup:

maria: Thanks — created a short runbook note under EncryptOps -> "propagation-window" with recommended mitigations and added the affected restores to backlog for follow-up.

pete: One action item: add ephemeral grant TTL telemetry and a histogram of grant-creation-to-first-object-write in the console so ops can set safe wait windows.

nishant: Agreed. I'll open an RFC for the manifest metadata change and quick telemetry patch.

sam: assigned myself to the staging replay and will ping here when done.
